generation_review.prompt:
Draw exactly ONE new Small Seal font glyph from the attached reference image. It shows FOUR historical specimen slots of the SAME character labelled THX, CCZ, QJZ and DYC; any slot marked UNAVAILABLE is absent evidence. Study ALL AVAILABLE specimens equally. Reconstruct one coherent attested whole form with the original ancient identity; do not combine incompatible variant components, imitate only THX, or substitute a modern Chinese character.

Build genuine smooth stroke trajectories as original harmonious Gothic monoline drawing, with absolutely CONSTANT stroke width around 3% of the full canvas. All strokes must share that width, with round caps and round joins, smooth rounded curves and precise straight bars, no taper, swelling, brush outlines, serifs, pressure modulation, textures or blobs. Keep every required counter and gap clearly open. Essential bar length relationships, branches, descending legs, tiny detached marks and contacts are structural requirements, not decoration.

Use a square 1:1 canvas. Center the ONE glyph inside the central70% with generous clear margins. Output ONLY pure BLACK constant-width strokes on a fully TRANSPARENT background, with no labels, text, codepoint, chart, grid, background, frame, shadows, watermark or multiple specimens. Exactly one complete glyph.

FINAL correction attempt: preserve exact historical course structure; no invented three-prong crown.
U+3D071 COMPLETE glyph. Left: one vertical stem carrying three horizontal bars, bottom longest and middle shortest. Middle: top is a TWO-PRONG V/FORK (one diagonal up-left, one diagonal up-right) with TWO SHORT HORIZONTAL OUTWARD ARMS at its lower sides. NO THIRD CENTRAL UPRIGHT above the fork: NOT a trident, NOT a pitchfork. The fork's lower stem joins a large smooth rounded arch. Arch left course ends freely midway down; arch right course curves down-left into a long vertical tail, so arch stays OPEN below. A separate small U with two upper prongs and one crossbar inside that arch creates ONE lower closed counter, no extra counter.

Right: tall upright at top carries one short rightward arm. Below it a longer horizontal bends to right and down into a large bulge; the bulge RETURNS DIAGONALLY DOWN-LEFT. A different short curved hook inside the bulge bends rightward/downward and continues into a LONG VERTICAL DOWNSTEM. Those two courses CROSS near the bulge's lower left. CRITICALLY the outer returning diagonal CONTINUES LEFT OF THIS CROSSING and ENDS AS A VISIBLE FREE DOWN-LEFT TIP. Do not stop the outer diagonal at the crossing. Right top short arm stays separate in height from lower bent bar. All four specimens show the top two-prong fork and the right crossing/branch inventory. Keep free lower-left end of middle arch; do not attach its outside to right component. Choose coherent open THX-type form.
